findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment: 1) Observed raw chicken and bacon in the walk in cooler stored above celerey and cheese. 2) Observed raw chicken and beef stored above cooked chicken wings in the reach in cooler. Raw chicken was moved during the inspection so that raw foods were not stored above ready to eat foods. 3-302.11  (P)  Store ready to eat foods above raw animal products to protect from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed nine portions of cheese/queso sitting on top of the lids of items in the steam table that were probed at 115F. Employee states that when they are busy, they pull these to warm up before they microwave them to serve. He states they pull these and use within 10 minutes but is not keeping any documentation of this. These were discarded and hot holding was discussed. 3-501.16(A)(1)  (P) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 135°F, or above. Reviewed hot holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(1).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: 1) Observed hot dogs with a date of 3/15 in the prep cooler. 2) Observed coleslaw, cooked onion/peppers and spinach dip with no date and an avocado mix dated 3/15 in the reach in cooler. 3) Observed hot dogs dated 3/15 in the walk in cooler. These are all open, ready to eat foods that must be date marked with the date of opening or preparation and held no longer than 7 days maximum with the date of opening/prep counting as a full Day 1. These items were discarded.  3-501.17  (Pf) Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment: Observed a bucket of road salt near the door that was not labeled with the name of the product. Person in charge labeled the container. Reference 7-102.11.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment: Observed traditional chicken wings in a bucket cooling in the reach in cooler to be probed at 125F and boneless wings in this same cooler to be probed at 95F with no indication as to when the cooling process began. Cooling must be done rapidly as an active process where it is documented when the cooling process begins to ensure that foods are reaching 70F within 2 hours of cooling. Facility has thermometers available and will begin tracking this. 3-501.15  (Pf) The method of cooling is inadequate. Use one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Discussed HACCP concept with the person in charge. Reference 3-501.15.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment: REPEAT PRACTICE> Observed a couple wet wiping cloths sitting on prep surfaces and cloths in the sanitizer bucket to not be fully submerged in sanitizer solution. Store wet wiping cloths submerged in sanitizer solution in between use.  3-304.14  (C) In-use wiping cloths are not stored properly. Cloths used for wiping spills shall be maintained dry. Cloths used to wipe surfaces and equipment shall be held in proper sanitizer solution. Cloths in-use for wiping surfaces in contact with raw animal foods shall be kept separate from cloths used for other purposes. In-use cloths must be laundered daily. Reference 3-304.14.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment: Observed small cups being stored in diced tomatoes in the prep cooler and in coleslaw in the reach in cooler. In use utensils should have a handle with the handle stored up and out of the food if stored in the food in between use.  3-304.12  (C)  Store in-use utensils: 1) in the food with the handle above the top of the food item; 2) on a clean and sanitized surface; 3) in running water; 4) in a container of hot water maintained at or above 135 °F. Reference 3-304.12.

The volume of cheese and dressing was reduced to keep the level in the containers at the line of ice to help keep the food at 41 degrees or less.
See page 2, " General Comments" for violation citations.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Raw hamburger was stored above pre-cooked food in the 3 door cooler.   A pan of raw chicken was stored above cooked pork loins in the walk-in cooler.  The containers of raw hamburger and chicken were both stored on bottom shelves below pre-cooked and ready-to-eat food, to CORRECT the violation.
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
(A) A bucket of meat was on the floor in the walk-in cooler.  (B) The ice bin in the waitress station was left open even though there were few customers in the store at the time of the inspection.   (C) Cooked bacon in the kitchen was uncovered.  The bucket of meat was elevated above the floor, the lid to the ice bin was closed, and the bacon was put in a covered container to CORRECT the violations.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
A spatula with food on it was not stored on the hot surface to prevent contamination.  The spatula was stored on the hot surface of the grill to CORRECT the violation.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: (A) The gaskets on the middle and right door of the 3-door cooler were torn.  Replace the gaskets.  (B) The lower shelf to the right of the 3-pan sink (on which chemicals are stored) was soiled/corroded.  Clean, sand, and paint the shelf.  (C) The lower shelf on the center island across from the grill was soiled/corroded.  Clean, sand, and paint the shelf.  (D) There was a gap between the kitchen handsink and wall.   Seal the gap.    750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Two buckets of sanitizer in the kitchen used to wipe down food prep surfaces were at 0 ppm sanitizer.  The buckets were re-filled with sanitizer that was 200 ppm quaternary ammonia.  If using chlorine sanitizer, mix the chlorine to 100 ppm which is about a quarter cap of bleach in the small buckets.  Use your test strips to check sanitizer concentrations in the buckets and dish machine.
750-800b To prevent cross-contamination, kitchenware and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed and sanitized after each use and following any interruption of operations during which time contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
(A) The two pizza oven racks were soiled.   (B) The water nozzle on the tea machine behind the bar was soiled.   Clean and sanitize the racks and nozzle.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
See page 2, "GENERAL COMMENTS" for violations.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

750-1110d Toilet facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair and free of objectionable odors. A supply of toilet tissue shall be provided at each toilet at all times. Easily cleanable, covered receptacles shall be provided for waste materials.

findings.title: Containers covered, adequate number, insect and rodent proof, emptied at proper intervals, clean

750-1130a Garbage and refuse shall be kept in durable easily cleanable, insect-proof, and rodent-proof containers.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment:
The exterior door by the bar would not close all the way on its own.  Repair the door so it is SELF CLOSING and TIGHT FITTING.
750-1170 Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
(1) The following floors were soiled:  (A) walk-in cooler under the stacks of beer by the door,   (B) electric panel room,   (C) mop sink room,    (D) under dish machine and 3-pan sink up close to the wall (REPEAT VIOLATION).  Clean these floors.
(2) A piece of coving is missing on the wall to the right of the exterior door in the kitchen (REPEAT VIOLATION).  Replace the coving.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.   750-1200 The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: (1) The following walls were soiled:  (A) above the mop sink,   (B) down low behind the dish machine and 3-pan sink (REPEAT VIOLATION),  (C) kitchen exterior door (also corroded) and threshold to the door,   (D) door to the electric panel room,   (E) wall in room with mop sink that opens to the kitchen.   Clean these walls.      (2) There are holes in the following walls:  (A) above and behind the 3-pan sink,  (B) doorway to kitchen in room with mop sink.  Seal the holes.  (3) The metal dividers one either side of the urinals are rusty on the bottoms. (REPEAT VIOLATION).  Sand and paint the bottoms of the panels.   750.1210a and 750.1220a

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.citation_text: 750.100 & 140 - A) Hot pink spray bottle of water in kitchen was not labeled as to the contents. Label all bottles and containers as to the contents, including water used during food prep. B) Cooling chicken strips and chicken poppers were not labeled with time and date. Chicken strips were below 70F and poppers were just fried and still at 188F. Proper labeling of cooked/cooling foods was discussed and poppers were placed in an ice bath to continue cooling. PHF shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41F.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text: 750.120 & 151 - (x2) A) Top layers of chicken and hamburgers in containers in an ice bath were at 52F-54F. Products in lower portion of containers in direct contact with ice were at 41F/below. All product out of temperature was discarded in the trash. Maintain cold potentially hazardous foods (PHF) at 41F/below at all times. Ice baths need to surround the outside of containers as high up as the depth of the food on the inside to ensure proper cold holding. B) Hotdogs in walkin cooler had date of 11/12. Hotdogs were discarded in the trash. Ready to eat, potentially hazardous foods must be dated and used or discarded within 7 days.

findings.title: Foods properly cooled
findings.comment: 750.140b - Queso in 3 door cooler had internal temperature ranging from 72F-84F. A clear explanation as to why the product was at such a high temperature could not be established. Manager was unsure why it was in the cooler because it was out for service earlier. Taking that into consideration and the fact that there was no time on the cover to indicate cooling process, the queso was discarded in the trash. Properly cool cooked PHF from 135F to 70F w/in 2 hrs and from 70F to 41F/below w/in 4 hrs. Use ice baths, stir frequently, and monitor the cooling temperatures and time with clean, calibrated stem thermometers to ensure foods are cooled properly. (Quick Chill Methods handout provided)

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text: 750.130 - Raw meats were observed stored over/next to ready to eat foods in coolers. Products were rearranged so raw foods were separate from ready to eat. All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above/away from raw foods. All raw meat shall be properly stored in order of cooking requirements with the lowest temperatures on the top shelf and the highest required temperature products on the bottom. (proper placement of raw foods in cold holding handout provided)

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.citation_text: 770.120 - A) Ice bin at wait station soda machine was open and drinks were not being prepared. Close the lid to the ice bin between uses during slow periods to protect ice from potential contamination. B) Box of ketchup packets was on the floor in the bar. Elevate boxes of foods, including single service condiments, up off the floor at least 6 inches. C) Cooked bacon in kitchen was uncovered. Keep foods covered between uses. Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Foods handled with minimal manual contact
findings.citation_text: 750.160 - (R) A) Styrofoam cups were observed inside 5 gallon buckets of wing sauce. B) Single service dressing cup was observed inside container of slaw in the 3 door cooler. Use proper equipment for dispensing foods (i.e. scoops or cups with handles, ladles, etc). Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750.160b - Employee observed adjusting clothing while wearing single use gloves and then returned to food prep without washing hands and putting on a new pair of gloves. Handwashing and glove use were discussed with employees and management. Gloves are intended for only one use and must be discarded when they are damaged, soiled, or there is an interruption in tasks. Always wash hands properly before putting on gloves and between glove changes. (when to wash hands and single-use gloves handouts provided)

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750.650a - Multiple plastic lids and containers were severely cracked. Replace all plastic lids and containers that are damaged. findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.citation_text: 750.830 - Dish machine at 0ppm chlorine. Calls for service were made after manager tried making repairs/priming the machine (sanitizer tubing had fallen loose at top of dish machine). Service call is scheduled to occur before Thursday. Manager and staff were advised the dish machine may be used for washing/rinsing but sanitizing step must be done in a compartment of the 3 part sink after the sinks have been thoroughly cleaned/sanitized (sanitizer in sink: 50ppm chlorine or 200ppm Quat). All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.citation_text: 750.810 - A) Wet wiping cloths observed out on counters in kitchen. Store wiping cloths in sanitizer solution between uses to inhibit the growth of microorganisms. When wiping cloths are no longer needed store them in proper soiled linen storage container. B) Bucket of sanitizer solution was at 100ppm Quat. Solution was remade and tested at proper concentration. Maintain Quat sanitizer solutions at 200ppm. Change solutions every 2-4 hours or more often if wiping cloths and solutions become heavily soiled.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.citation_text: 750.240 - Jumbo hotdogs were observed thawing in the wash compartment of the kitchen 3 part sink. The sink had been filled with water, plugged, and the water was shut off. Hotdogs were removed from the sink, placed in clean containers and moved to walkin cooler to finish thawing process. Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following methods: 1. Under refrigeration 41F/below, 2. Under potable running water 70F/below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, or 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
